newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Extracts from Yeltsin radio address.
newsitem.headline: Extracts from Yeltsin radio address.

text.p: Following are extracts of the radio address given by Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday and translated by Reuters.

I have been receiving lots of letters with wishes for a quick recovery. A lot of warm and friendly words have been addressed to (my wife) Naina and me. I want to thank you all for your support and care. This helps me now. I am getting ready for the (heart) operation, something that takes a lot of time. But I am in touch with what is going on in the country. I am helped by a strong team of professionals.

Sometimes one gets the impression that while most think about the future of Russia and try to do their best to change life for the better, some see the President's illness as a pretext for not doing anything, working for their own benefit and spawning petty intrigues. I said before the elections and repeat now -- don't rush to change the portraits. The country has a president and an active president at that!

Chechnya ranks top of the many problems that have to be dealt with today. Important shifts in the situation there are taking place. My aide Alexander Lebed fulfilled my instruction and stopped the military conflict. The most important thing is he succeeded in stopping the bloodshed. But it is too soon to stop worrying. The separatists are approaching negotiations very reluctantly. We must get prisoners home very quickly.
I am very worried about the situation in the armed forces.

I am taking this issue under special control. Russia must have a modern and professional army. Serving in it must be a source of respect and prestige, both for the man in the ranks and to the officer. We will achieve this.
SENDING OFFICIALS TO SCHOOLS TO EXPLAIN RUSSIA'S HISTORY

I have asked government members, (Prime Minister) Viktor Stepanovich Chernomyrdin, governors, mayors to visit schools and teach an ordinary lesson there. Let them talk about the history of new Russia and answer questions.

I especially appeal to schoolchildren. Do not be afraid of your superiors and ask them the most pointed questions, you have every right to do this. Write to me and tell me how the lesson went. You are our future."
